chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan and Muhammad ibn Sinan, all from Ibn Muskan, from al-Halbi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the woman who gifts herself to the man who marries her without a dower. He said: 'This was only for the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). As for others, this is not correct until he compensates her with something, which he presents to her before he consummates the marriage with her, whether little or much, even if it is a garment or a dirham.'
And he (peace be upon him) said: 'The dirham suffices.'

key_terms.يَدْخُلَ بِهَا: He consummates the marriage (enters with her)

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum requirement for a valid marriage if a woman gifts herself without a specified dowry?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the distinction between the unique privilege of the Prophet Muhammad, who could accept a wife's self-gift without dower, and the general rule for others requiring at least a symbolic mahr (such as a dirham or garment) prior to consummation. It underscores the Shia juristic principle that while the essence of marriage is mutual consent, the dower remains a mandatory right of the wife to ensure the contract's validity and financial security.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Safwan and Muhammad Bin Sinan, altogether from Ibn Muskan, from Al Halby who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the woman who gifts herself to the man who marries her without a dower. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But rather, this was for the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>, and as for the others, so this is not correct until he places something for her and sends it to her before he copulates with her, be it little or more, and even if it is a garment, or one Dirham’.
en.sarwar: 1. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan and Muhammad ibn ‘Isma’il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn Sinan all from ibn Muskan from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a woman who gives herself as a gift to a man for marriage.

He (the Imam) said, ‘This was only for the Holy Prophet, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, but for others it is not proper without something in exchange before going to bed with her; a small or large amount even a cloth or dirham.’
